A.name: The Bandit Queen
A.prompt:
A frame from a 1920s period feature film on 35mm motion-picture film. The place is the bank steps in the attached frame from the film: keep its stone columns, the wide steps, the dusk sky, the fireball in the doorway and the banknotes drifting through the air. All six masked men from that frame stay, every one of them, in the same order from left to right: PLUM, BOTTLE, CRIMSON in his black fedora, MARINE, RUST and SILVER, suits and masks copied exactly from the attached line-up card. They have closed up into a tight wall one step behind her, big and broad, gloved fists at their sides, looming like bodyguards. In front of them, centre frame and nearest the lens, stands the seventh member and the gang's leader: a small, slight woman, a head and a half shorter than any of the men, seen whole from head to boots. She carries no weapon. She wears a black velvet riding habit: a short fitted jacket buttoned to the throat, and a long full skirt sweeping to small laced riding boots. A black Stetson with a curling black ostrich plume, slightly too big for her, sits on the balaclava. Black kid gauntlets to the forearm. Her jet-black knitted balaclava covers her whole head and neck with no eye, nose or mouth openings and tucks into her collar; a large white ring is stitched round the whole face, and one small red triangle with rounded corners, pointing down, sits high inside the ring on the right-hand side of the picture. Chin up, one hand on her hip, the other arm thrust out with her index finger pointing straight at the lens. Low camera at her chest height, 28mm lens, so the men tower behind her. No text, lettering or logos anywhere. 16:9.

Thanks.
